issues.title: Filling a fluid container from a tank destroys the fluid in creative mode
issues.body:
Filling a fluid container from a tank in creative mode can silently destroy the fluid. The block's tank drains but the filled container never reaches you. In survival the same interaction is fine.

The easiest way to see it is with a plain water bucket, because it takes two clicks and it's the second one that loses fluid.

1. Creative mode. Place a tank block that uses Mantle's fluid transfer for its right-click behaviour (I used a Tinkers' Construct seared fuel gauge) and put 2000 mb of water in it.
2. Make sure you have no water bucket anywhere in your inventory, and hold an empty bucket.
3. Right-click the tank. The tank goes 2000 -> 1000 and a water bucket turns up in your inventory. Fine so far, though note it lands in the inventory rather than your hand.
4. Right-click the tank again. The tank empties, but you still have only the one water bucket.

That second click destroyed 1000 mb. If you already happen to be carrying a matching filled container when you start, the very first click destroys it instead, which is what makes it easy to hit without noticing.

I read the tank with `/data get block <x> <y> <z> tank` and counted buckets with `/clear @s minecraft:water_bucket 0`, which counts without removing anything. The same sequence in survival with two empty buckets conserves everything: tank 2000 -> 1000 -> empty and two water buckets at the end.

It isn't specific to buckets. I first ran into this with a Tinkers tool that has a tank, where a single right-click ate the whole 2000 mb because the filled tool had nowhere to go.

What I expected: creative shouldn't consume my empty bucket, but the fluid the tank gave up should end up somewhere. That's what vanilla does when you scoop up a water source in creative — the source is removed, you keep the empty bucket, and a water bucket is added to your inventory.

Where it seems to come from: `FluidTransferHelper.interactWithContainer` fills a copy of the held stack and hands the result to `ItemUtils.createFilledResult(stack, player, filled)`. The three argument form defaults to preventing duplicates, and for a creative player that branch returns the held stack unchanged and only adds the filled container if `Inventory#contains` doesn't already find an identical stack. It also ignores whether the add succeeded, so a full inventory loses it too. The tank drain has already been executed by that point, so any time the result is dropped the fluid goes with it. The same call appears twice in that method, once on the JSON fluid transfer path and once on the capability path.

Versions: Mantle `1.20` branch at 2c99fcf8, Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47.4.0. Tinkers' Construct was only there to supply a tank block — the item side of the repro above is a vanilla bucket.

issues.title: [Bug] Books do not use English translation when others are missing
issues.body:
### Current book behaviour
The `BookData` loads language files in a book repository ***only*** for current language.
This causes that, when some of the translations in a language file is missing, the book directly use the raw translation key, instead of considering to find the ones in the `en_us.lang`.
(According to the source code, this bug still exists. (At least it exists in 1.20.1, 1.11.79))

### Expected behaviour
When one translation key in a certain language is missing, the book should look it up in the `en_us.lang`. If still not found, use the raw translation key.

### Possible solution
Let the book read `en_us.lang` at the same time when reloading resouce packs.

issues.title: `SmartItemHandlerSlot` ignores the stack size of the item itself, bypassing stack limit restrictions, allowing you to stack unstackable items up to 64

labels.description: Affects Minecraft versions 1.18

issues.body:
### Reproduction steps:

1) Place a crafting station (from Tinker's Construct) adjacent to a Chest
2) Open the crafting station.
3) Observe you can stack items up to 64 in the chest, even items that should not normally stack, and bypass all stack size restrictions:

![ticon](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35673674/232862310-1ae64a67-da18-4cd7-a462-904f85591f25.png)

### Mods:

- Minecraft 1.18.2
- Forge 40.2.1
- Mantle 1.9.43
- Tinkers Construct 3.6.3.111

### Logs: [debug.log](https://github.com/SlimeKnights/Mantle/files/11264801/debug.log)

### Explanation

This method:

https://github.com/SlimeKnights/Mantle/blob/97f6c8e17ccb14d0a76f20547d39a784428a01d6/src/main/java/slimeknights/mantle/inventory/SmartItemHandlerSlot.java#L13-L16

is an incomplete implementation. The vanilla implementation here takes the minimum of **both** the slot's stack size limit, and the item stack's size limit. This does not consider stack dependent slot restrictions, and as a result enables bypassing vanilla behavior using the crafting station.

What that *should* read, is:

```java
@Override 
public int getMaxStackSize(ItemStack stack) { 
    return Math.min(stack.getMaxStackSize(), getItemHandler().getSlotLimit(getSlotIndex())); 
} 
```

Reduced protection levels:

Packages and renames:

issues.title: RenderGameOverlayEvent.Post not fired after Mantle heart rendering.

labels.name: resolved
labels.description: Fixed in code, not yet released

issues.body:
Forge usually fires a RenderGameOverlayEvent.Post (with ElementType.HEALTH) after drawing the player's hearts. Since Mantle replaces heart rendering by cancelling RenderGameOverlayEvent.Pre, this event is never fired, so post-health rendering never occurs.

It'd be nice if Mantle fired a RenderGameOverlayEvent.Post at the end of its own health rendering to support other mods' custom heart rendering and overlays.

issues.title: Oredict lookup in RecipeMatch.OreDict creates empty ore entries
issues.body:
**Minecraft Version**
1.12.2

**Mantle Version**
1.3.3.56

**Versions of Mantle dependant mods**
Tinkers' Construct 2.13.0.184

**Forge version/build**
14.23.5.2847

**Versions of any mods potentially related to the issue**
CodeChickenLib 3.2.3.358

When a `RecipeMatch.OreDict` instance is created (e.g. by registering a match for a Tinkers' Construct material), [the constructor looks up matching items](https://github.com/SlimeKnights/Mantle/blob/2a0b45038b14b59f5e2efe5157441987ae0091c8/src/main/java/slimeknights/mantle/util/RecipeMatch.java#L289) using a call to `OreDictionary::getOres(String name)`. However, this function will always register the ore name in the ore dictionary regardless of whether the caller intends to register items under that name or not. This causes issues such as phantamanta44/tinkers-evolution#8, where other mods check for the existence of an ore by the existence of the ore name; see TheCBProject/CodeChickenLib#303.

I propose replacing the call with `OreDictionary.getOres(oredictEntry, false)` to prevent the creation of the ore name on lookup. I'll also open a separate issue on the Tinkers' Construct repository to address the same problem with ore dictionary lookups there.

issues.title: Health bar doesn't support Forge left_height
issues.body:
If the value of `GuiIngameForge.left_height` is not set to 39 directly before drawing the health bar, Mantle ignores the actual value and just draws the health bar in the same location. This causes an incompatibility with my mod Better HUD: mccreery/better-hud#30, which modifies the value of `left_height`.

Repro:
- Install Mantle and Better HUD
- Open the Better HUD menu with U and disable everything
- Enable just the health bar

You'll see that the health bar shows offset from the bottom of the screen, even though `left_height` is set so that it should render at the bottom.

issues.title: Add and option to disable ExtraHeartRenderHandler
issues.body: Currently the ExtraHeartRenderHandler takes priority over other mods attempts at rendering the health bar, so any mod that tries to implement its own custom health bar on screen, is replaced with the vanilla looking 10 heart bar forced by mantle. This breaks UIs with other mods and could be prevented if there was an option to disable the 10 heart force render if a modpack wanted to use another mod to display health on screen.

issues.title: [1.11 (+?)] Modifierless jar on Maven is deobfuscated!
issues.body:
The normal jar on the maven is deobfuscated, causing all kinds of problems when used in a dev env with a different mapping!

I suggest adding
```Groovy
jar {
    // Do whatever you need here...

    finalizedBy reobfJar
}
```
to your `build.gradle`.

Also see MinecraftForge/ForgeGradle#440

I don't know which versions this affects though. Might be a lot though.

issues.title: [1.12+] Guava Dependency Problems
issues.body:
Hey there, at the moment I'm playing around with updating TinkersToolLeveling to 1.12 and learning a bit more about Tinkers in general. But I quickly ran into a problem with Mantle since it currently uses version 3.2 of the configurate library which is compiled against version 17 of Guava. The 1.12 update of Minecraft however now uses version 21 of Guava and in my case this means, that the following crash occurs [CrashLog](https://gist.github.com/tommyTT/a1a2ea2ba339ae84e1cbe9d5217b6d61).

It looks like updating the dependency to version 3.3 worked fine for my local version, but more testing is required. [Configurate Commit](https://github.com/zml2008/configurate/commit/11d0d3bca9df4b6cbcb8a03480486c7173c9784a)

Regards,
Tommy

issues.title: Integrate new opportunities in Mantle
issues.body:
For example, Custom Ore Gen is very interesting mod which help very much customize your modpacks. For example now, I create TerraFirmaCraft+GregTech modpack, but I can't use cog because it's to hard and unstable. Integrate please lite version of this mod in Mantle, for example, it doesn't have custom gui and all configuration are in config file. You can disable vanilla ores and ores from mod and for example something like this (config file):
********************
VeinName(###)
Biomes:###^#, #####^#
Ore:###^#, ###^#
Height:###^###
VHeight:###
Area:##
Mass:###
Density:###
********************

********************
VeinName(GalenaOre)
Biomes: ExtremeHills^60, Forest^40
Ore: Galena^70, Antimony^30
Height: 40^80
VHeight:8
Area:3
Mass:40
Density:2
********************
What this means? This means that in world will be generated ore vein with name “GalenaOre” with frequency 40/(40+n)*100%(“n” is mass of other veins). It will be spawn in biome ExtremeHills with frequency 60% or Forest with frequency 40%. It will be comprise 70% of Galena ore and 30% of Antimony ore (users must write in this pole id of some ores). It will be spawn on height 40-80(with the biggest frequency in the middle). Height of this vein in blocks is 8 and it will spawn on area 3^3. His density will be 2 blocks of ore per one block of cobble. All veins are cubic. In addition, if you choose to do so, please add this feature in previous versions of Mantle.

issues.title: Pulse's defaultEnable option ignored if mod is not loaded
issues.body:
Scenario: Start out in a fresh instance with Tinkers Construct installed and Crafting Tweaks **not** installed, with no configs generated yet.

This line right here will generate the config option for the Pulse, using PulseMeta.getEnabled():
[ForgeCFG.java#L52](https://github.com/SlimeKnights/Mantle/blob/bcc4586d5d0bceb0a6d5d96341353ee842db3cf9/src/main/java/slimeknights/mantle/pulsar/config/ForgeCFG.java#L52)

However, PulseMeta.enabled has been set to false because the mod wasn't loaded here:
[PulseManager.java#L148](https://github.com/SlimeKnights/Mantle/blob/84a2615f4a5634e62ac53a6ed4e92aaaba802996/src/main/java/slimeknights/mantle/pulsar/control/PulseManager.java#L148)

...resulting in the value for the newly generated config option to be false despite defaultEnable claiming the default would be true. This makes it painful to add Crafting Tweaks to a pack later on as users have to specifically enable it in the Tinkers Construct config.

I believe this could be easily fixed by making ForgeCFG.isModuleEnabled use meta.isEnabledDefault() instead of meta.isEnabled() for the default value of the config option.
